newsitem.title: UK: Ousted Conservative MP launches court fight.
newsitem.headline: Ousted Conservative MP launches court fight.

text.p: A ruling Conservative member of parliament who was ousted by his constituency party last week for disloyalty to Prime Minister John Major on Wednesday launched a court fight to overturn the decision.

Sir George Gardiner said his lawyers had issued a High Court writ against his local party association in Reigate, to the south of London, which last Thursday voted to take away his right to defend his parliamentary seat for the Conservatives.

Gardiner, 61, a leading Eurosceptic opposed to moves towards European integration, was ditched after describing Major as "a ventriloquist's dummy". He said on Wednesday he was seeking a declaration that last week's constituency association vote was invalid.

He said he was also seeking a court injunction to prevent the Reigate Conservative Association choosing a new candidate to fight the seat for the party at the election which Major must call by May at the latest.

Senior Conservatives are worried that Gardiner, who had a safe 17,664-vote majority at the last election in 1992 and has represented Reigate in parliament since 1974, could decide to stand as an independent if he is not reinstated.
If he did, this could split the vote in his constituency, handing victory to the opposition.

The opposition Labour Party are leading the Conservatives by around 20 points in polls and a Reuter survey of predictions by experts issued on Wednesday predicted a 48-seat Labour majority. -- London Newsroom +44-171-542-7768
